newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai to sell part of securities house.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai to sell part of securities house.

text.p: Hyundai Electronics, an affiliate of South Korea's Hyundai Group, said on Monday it would sell a 30.93 percent stake in Citizens Investment Trust Management and Securities Co Ltd to a Canadian bank.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, a leading Canadian investment bank, will buy the shares for $175 million, becoming the biggest single shareholder in the South Korean securities house.
The sale is expected to be completed in mid-June.
Hyundai Group would remain the biggest shareholder with two affiliates owning a combined stake of 36.86 percent, a Hyundai Electronics official said.
The official said Hyundai Electronics' stake in Citizens Investment would be reduced to 21.63 percent with the sale. Hyundai Securities holds 15.23 percent.
He said Hyundai Electronics was making the sale to raise money to invest in non-memory production.

Citizens Investment, a major domestic institutional investor formerly known as Citizens Investment Trust Management Co, in March expanded into securities and merchant banking after Hyundai became the biggest shareholder. It earlier had concentrated on trust business.
